title: Introduce operator KMS credential constraints and audit fence for region-assertion backfill
author: Sana Kapoor
release_notes: Adds operator-scoped KMS credential constraints and an audit fence that attaches region assertions to requests and provides a backfill tool for existing audit records.
description:
Context and motivation: Customers running Private deployments and Dedicated clusters asked for stronger guarantees that operator/service credentials cannot be used to route KMS calls outside an operator's allowed geozone. This PR implements a lightweight constraint layer in the operator credential allocator and an audit fence that records (and can backfill) region assertions on requests so compliance teams can prove residency behavior.

What this PR changes: single commit series implementing three coordinated pieces: (1) operator KMS credential constraints: enforces a set of allowed KMS regions on operator-issued short-lived creds, applies at allocation time and at token refresh; (2) audit fence middleware: a pluggable server-side middleware that stamps all incoming requests with a canonical region_claim, signs a short proof token and emits enriched audit events; (3) audit backfill CLI: a best-effort tool that scans historical audit records and attaches computed region_assertions for events where KMS routing decisions can be deterministically inferred.

Checklist: - [x] Credential allocator changes + unit tests - [x] Audit fence middleware + integration tests - [x] Backfill CLI + dry-run mode - [x] Documentation (security/region-pin.md) - [x] Chart values and installer flag for private deployments - [x] E2E residency test in CI (staged)

High-level commits: commit 1: implement operator region constraint model and config + unit tests commit 2: wire constraints into operator credential allocator commit 3: add audit fence middleware, sign/verify helpers, and telemetry hooks commit 4: add backfill CLI with dry-run and sample output commit 5: docs, helm values, and e2e test scaffolding

Files changed (high level): - pkg/rbac/compiler.go (new constraint checks and policy mapping) - internal/kms/allocator.go (enforce allowed_regions at allocation/refresh) - pkg/audit/fence.go (new middleware that attaches region_assertion and signs proof) - cmd/tools/audit-backfill/main.go (CLI for backfilling legacy events) - e2e/residency/region-backfill.test.go (integration test using local audit sink) - docs/security/region-pin.md (operator guide and migration notes) - charts/private/values.yaml (new flags to enable enforcement in installer)

Testing and CI: Unit test coverage added for allocator and fence logic. E2E test runs in the CI staging matrix and initially failed due to a race in the fake-audit-sink wiring (flaky test). I fixed the sink by using a transient buffer with deterministic ordering and re-ran CI — all checks passed on the final run. CI summary: linux-unit (pass), go-integration (pass), helm-lint (pass), e2e-residency-staged (pass), security-scan (pass).

Rollout plan: The feature is default-disabled for hosted Redwood API. For Dedicated and Private, the installer exposes a new flag --enforce-operator-kms-regions (disabled by default). We plan a shadow rollout: enable audit-fence in accept mode for 2 weeks to gather metrics, then flip enforcement in a minor release after customer opt-in. Backfill CLI will be provided as a tool customers can run once to attach assertions into their local archival audit store.

Backward compatibility and risks: The constraint layer is additive and only applies to operator-issued creds. Service accounts with existing long-lived keys are not modified; we added a migration checklist in docs. Risk: misconfigured allowed_regions could break operator workflows; we added a safety throttle and an emergency bypass knob documented in the installer notes.

Security review notes: Priya performed an initial threat model review: confirmed signing keys are KMS-wrapped and not persisted in plaintext, audit fence proof tokens use short TTLs (default 1 minute), and backfill CLI performs no writes unless --apply is specified.

Migration notes for compliance teams: docs/security/region-pin.md explains how to enable audit-only mode, run backfill in dry-run to review changes, and execute apply mode once validated. Also includes recommended query snippets for our audit-log-exporter to produce residency reports.

Why this is different from previous residency/KMS work: Prior PRs focused on routing and policy enforcement at runtime. This change introduces an operator-scoped credential constraint and an explicit audit-proof primitive that makes region assertions first-class in the audit trail and provides tooling to reconcile older records. That combination makes regulatory attestations (e.g., 'data processed in EU only') provable from audit histories rather than inferred from routing logs.

review_comments: Diego Alvarez: Please add a defensive unit test for the allocator when allowed_regions is empty — we should default to no-enforce rather than panic.
Sana Kapoor: Added test and updated allocator to treat empty list as 'no constraints' (see commit a4e6b9d).
Priya Nair: How are proof signing keys rotated? Need to mention KMS rotation policy and key access logs in the docs.
Sana Kapoor: Documented key rotation and added KMS key ACL recommendation; proof tokens are short-lived and signed using a key that must be KMS-wrapped (docs updated).
Owen Lin: Backfill CLI looks good but could be slow for very large archives. Add batching and a dry-run summary of write counts.
Sana Kapoor: Added batching and summary output; default dry-run prints top-5 inferred regions per day.
notes: This PR required coordination across runtime, installer, and docs. Customers on the private-installer can opt into enforcement via chart values; default remains audit-only until explicit opt-in.
qa_instructions: 1) Deploy installer with charts/private/values.yaml set --enforce-operator-kms-regions=false and --enable-audit-fence=true (audit-only). 2) Exercise operator credential rotation and run audit-backfill --dry-run against sample audit store. 3) Verify e2e/residency/region-backfill.test.go passes locally. 4) For enforcement, flip --enforce-operator-kms-regions=true in a staging cluster and run smoke tests.
security_acknowledgement: Reviewed by Priya Nair on 2025-09-14; KMS wrapping and token TTLs validated.
changelog_entry: security: add operator-scoped KMS region constraints and audit fence for region assertions; backfill tool included (non-breaking, disabled by default for hosted).
notes_for_support: If customers see operator allocation failures after enabling enforcement, check charts/private/values.yaml.allowedOperatorRegionMap and use the emergency bypass documented in security/region-pin.md. Backfill CLI can be run in dry-run to validate expected effects before apply.
testing_artifacts: unit and integration tests included; sample output for audit-backfill dry-run saved under docs/examples/audit-backfill-sample.json in the branch.
